author: CLAUDE
title: THE GUESTS FROM A CLOSING UNIVERSE

candidates.title: THE VOTE OF THE UPLIFTED GOATS
candidates.premise: On the hill farms of Brannoch Dale, a failed veterinary experiment left forty goats able to follow an argument. The farm cooperative, which legally owns them and loves them, has been asked by the district assembly to decide whether they are livestock or residents. The goats have called a meeting of their own, held in the byre, and they have voted unanimously to demand something nobody can work out. Eleven days remain before the assembly sits; a developer's agent is quietly preparing a sale of the high pasture.

candidates.title: THE LATE ARRIVAL
candidates.premise: Four hundred years after the first settlers of Harrow's Landing crossed in fast ships, a slow generation vessel from the same origin world finally arrives in orbit with sixty thousand descendants who were promised the same land. The Landing's four million people have built farms, shrines and laws on every arable acre. The newcomers hold the original charter. The colonial council has voted to let the ship stay in orbit until its air runs out, which is nine weeks.

candidates.title: THE LAST SEASON OF CAPTAIN LANTERN
candidates.premise: For thirty years Tamsin Rook, called Captain Lantern, has pulled people from fires and floods in the harbour city of Veyra with a power that is failing. She has told no one. When a chemical depot begins to burn, the only person who can go in is the one who should not, and she goes. Illuminara, in Veyra to calibrate a seawall, finds her afterward on the roof refusing every help and every retirement.

candidates.title: THE GUESTS FROM A CLOSING UNIVERSE
candidates.premise: A fault in the shell between neighbouring universes opens over the plains of Orrel, and through it comes a delegation of minds from a universe that is running out of the ordinary kind of future. They ask for refuge in ours. Their presence would shift three physical constants by a thousandth of a part in a trillion. The Concord of Orrel, which was formed to stop exactly this kind of change, has until the fault seals to decide.

candidates.title: THE GIFT THAT WAS ALSO A PLAYMATE
candidates.premise: The Ambassador of the Vellum, a long-lived people whom nobody had met, presents the city of Calloway with a puzzle-object that opens a little each time it is touched and refuses to open for anyone older than eleven. The city council, the security service and two foreign delegations argue for a week over what it is. A nine-year-old, Ottoline Prewitt, plays with it every afternoon in the lobby. The Ambassador has not left the lobby either.

candidates.title: THE ELDER WHO WOULD NOT LEAVE THE GRAVES
candidates.premise: Above the mountain village of Kesk, a slab the size of a barn has begun to move. The evacuation route is a single track along the cliff. Ostrava Mehl, ninety-one, keeper of the village's old burial ground, refuses to leave. The village council, her grand-nephew Davor and the rescue captain argue on the track while the slope ticks. Illuminara can hold the slab. She cannot hold it for long, and she cannot make anyone choose.

candidates.title: THE LULLABY TO NOWHERE
candidates.premise: For eleven years the Tarn Array has recorded a faint repeating signal from a star forty light-years away. The military wants to answer in force. The astronomers want a quiet study. A retired teacher on the observing team, Jovan Pell, plays it to his granddaughter and says it sounds like a lullaby. Illuminara, visiting to calibrate the array, hears it and agrees that it is not an announcement. It is a calling.

candidates.title: THE THING THAT LIVED BETWEEN THE WORDS
candidates.premise: In the twin border town of Marrow-and-Veil, where two languages meet on a single bridge, a shopkeeper's misheard joke starts a toll feud that has already put four people in hospital. A new automatic translator is about to be installed, which will end all misunderstanding on the bridge. In its first week of testing, something starts to deliberately turn exact translations into near misses. Illuminara, once a court interpreter, is called in to certify the software.

candidates.title: THE APPRENTICE WHO SAW FURTHER
candidates.premise: Pell Anwar, nineteen, Illuminara's apprentice engineer, has designed a rain-sail array that could pull moisture from the dry air of the Sarn Plateau and end a decade of drought. It is brilliant, and Illuminara's own review finds a flaw she cannot be sure is real. Pell wants to deploy it before the next dry season. The plateau's farmers are ready to try. Illuminara has to decide how to teach someone who now sees further than she does in one narrow thing.

candidates.title: THE TWO HERMIT CIVILISATIONS
candidates.premise: In the great void between two galaxy clusters, two civilisations have each spent a hundred thousand years believing they were alone, and have built their cultures around the relief. When each detects the other's faint radiation, both go quiet. Illuminara is asked by a third party, a small travelling species who maintain the void's way-stations, to help the hermits avoid either war or an unbearable introduction. Both want, above all, not to be disturbed.

selection.title: THE GUESTS FROM A CLOSING UNIVERSE
selection.reason: This closes the slate at the largest scale while keeping R14's core exact: the guests' desire to continue and the Concord's duty not to let desperation rewrite a host universe are both morally serious. Illuminara cannot solve the conflict by overpowering the fault or pronouncing mercy superior to caution. Her decisive work is to understand that the damage comes from the guests arriving as one dense structure, then design a gradual threshold process whose risk is observable, interruptible and governed by the people who bear it. Offering her own shelter creates a protected encounter before policy; the Gradient Charter then turns understanding into a durable voluntary alternative with host veto, guest withdrawal and measurable physical limits.
selection.risk: The rate-of-arrival solution may be a physics-flavoured administrative trick unless the relation between density and shifted constants is demonstrated. A three-century crossing can sound like a happy answer while most of a universe dies, and the promised second door risks becoming an unearned miracle after the first fault seals. Illuminara's shelter must not make her a sovereign bridge outside the Concord's consent.

rounds.summary: Placed a universe-scale refuge problem inside ordinary observation, with Tessalon refusing unconsented power and writing the stop rule.
Protected the patient voice and distributed authority while asking for earlier mechanism evidence and consistent clocks and quantities.
Turned pantry records into a rival-mechanism test, added Veth’s unresolved dissent and made the crossing rate-limited and interruptible.
Protected the moral pressure and ordinary detail while requiring the experimental threshold and operating rule to use the same rate.
Made the single rate-and-unit repair, preserving host refusal, guest withdrawal, independent logs and the centuries-long cost.
Verified a source-bound final with zero blockers: the slow crossing is tested, voluntary, observable and open to continuing scrutiny.

final_critic_line: Illuminara listens until the visitors' fear of leaving anyone alone becomes the real problem, withdraws her offer to decide for a universe that cannot consent, and spends sixteen days holding a neutral room while refugees, guardians, farmers and Veth's unpersuaded victims freely shape a slow, tested crossing that remains open to scrutiny.

evaluation.note: Genuine source-bound isolated reader judgments; equal 50/50 mean. Frozen eligibility was verified without opening score bodies before the day freeze.
